messages:
sec-oncall: Deploy bot flagged a failure in the nightly base-image rebuild: cosign couldn't sign artifacts due to KMS permission DENIED. Opening thread to coordinate. https://ci.internal/rebuilds/4521 :warning:

deploy-bot: automatic retries exhausted (3/3), escalated to manual.

alina: digging into KMS logs now. Seeing AccessDeniedException for service account used by cosign at 02:41 UTC.

benjamin: I pushed an IAM tightening change yesterday to the KMS key policy for artifact signing. Might have removed the signer SA binding. Looping in infra.

luis: confirmed infra changed key policy to remove a broad binding; intended for least-privilege hardening. Didn't realize CI relies on svc-artifact directly.

jamie: audit-bot, pull all KMS allow/deny events and cosign stderr for the past 6 hours so we have an evidentiary trail.

audit-bot: Attached summary: kms_evt_987 DENY svc-artifact at 02:41 UTC, kms_evt_988 GRANT build-runner at 02:49 UTC. Cosign log: "2026-03-21T02:41:01Z cosign: exit 1 - rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = requestor not authorized".

alina: matches. CI cosign attempted with svc-artifact but key policy no longer includes that member.

benjamin: I removed the binding thinking signing would use the build-runner impersonation flow. CI still uses svc-artifact for cosign. My oversight.

sec-oncall: Impact: three images in staging missing attestations. No production deploys affected. Compliance gap for the release window.

jamie: Action plan (short): 1) restore minimal signer binding to svc-artifact (benjamin), 2) re-run cosign to create attestations (alina), 3) capture logs and timeline in incident tracker (sec-oncall), 4) add CI unit test for signer perms (luis). Can we complete initial fixes in 60m?

benjamin: restoring now. Command: gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding artifacts-key --location=global --keyring=redwood-keyring --member="serviceAccount:svc-artifact@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeySign"

alina: once binding is back, I'll re-run signing: for img in $(cat failed_images); do cosign sign --key kms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/redwood-keyring/cryptoKeys/artifacts-key@$img; done

benjamin: binding restored, gcloud returned etag update OK.

audit-bot: iam_evt_5643 recorded: iam policy change by benjamin@redwood at 02:52 UTC.

alina: re-run results: image-a signed ✅, image-b signed ✅, image-c signed ✅. Attestations pushed to staging registry.

sec-oncall: Good. Preliminary root cause: manual RBAC hardening removed the service account binding used by the CI signing job.

luis: Proposed remediations: 1) add KMS-affecting checklist to infra PR template, 2) implement CI signing test that exercises the KMS signing path against a test key and fails PRs that break it, 3) automate binding checks during key rotations.

jamie: short-term guardrail: add a preflight that triggers on IAM changes to artifacts-key/keyring to run a quick signing smoke test and notify #eng-release if it fails. Pseudocode: if iam_change.targets_key(artifacts-key): run_sign_test(test_image); if fail: block_merge_and_notify()

benjamin: I'll open an infra PR to codify the minimal binding and include rollback-safe notes. Also proposing to evaluate using impersonated short-lived credentials for cosign to reduce blast radius.

luis: Impersonation via Workload Identity/token exchange is a good medium-term fix; requires runner changes. I'll scope it as a follow-up.

alina: I logged incident 2026-03-21-4521 in tracker and attached cosign logs + KMS audit entries. Severity: S3 (compliance).

sec-oncall: Ownership: benjamin -> infra PR for binding and PR template change, luis -> CI signing test and spec for impersonation, alina -> artifact verification and incident attachments, jamie -> preflight notifier, sec-oncall -> writeup/timeline. Target: docs & tests merged by EOW.

deploy-bot: requeued build #4521 after manual sign.

benjamin: will post PR link when ready.

luis: picking up CI test first thing tomorrow.

jamie: will share notifier draft in #eng-release for feedback.

sec-oncall: closing thread - keep incident doc updated. If related failures crop up in 24h, reopen. :thumbsup:

alina: thanks everyone.
